I felt deeply disappointed by the way we were treated. The person managing the ashram was described to us as a temple priest, so I expected more kindness, honesty, and hospitality.
I request the concerned authorities, including the Varanasi administration and Uttar Pradesh government, to look into the conditions and management of such accommodation facilities so that other pilgrims do not face similar problems.
My sincere advice to fellow visitors: please check the facilities and reviews carefully before booking or paying in advance. Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend this place.
A visit to Kashi Vishwanath should begin with peace and devotion, not this kind of distressing experience.

▪️Karnataka HC granted visitation rights to a father to meet his daughter while his wife argued that he had failed to pay the entire maintenance amount of ₹60,000 p.m. awarded for her and their minor daughter.

▪️Court held that a father could not be denied the opportunity to maintain a relationship with his child merely because of a dispute concerning maintenance. It emphasised that welfare and best interests of the child must remain the paramount consideration while determining visitation rights.

▪️The parties got married on Dec 4, 2017, and their daughter was born on Jan 30, 2019. Following matrimonial disputes, wife filed a petition seeking dissolution of marriage on grounds of adultery and desertion. During the pendency of matrimonial proceedings, husband filed an application u/s 26 HMA, seeking visitation rights to meet their daughter, who was residing with wife.

▪️The trial court awarded maintenance of ₹40,000 p.m. to wife, which was subsequently enhanced by Karnataka HC to ₹60,000 p.m. for the wife and child. On Feb 3, 2025, trial court allowed husband’s application for visitation, permitting him to meet the child twice a month for 3 hours, make daily video calls for 10 minutes from Monday to Friday, attend school events, meet the child on her birthday, and keep her with him for 10 days during summer vacation.

▪️Challenging trial court’s order, wife contended that husband had failed to comply with the maintenance order, having paid only a portion of the amount towards the child’s maintenance while leaving her own maintenance unpaid. 

▪️She argued that husband should not be permitted to exercise visitation rights until outstanding maintenance had been paid. She also objected to daily video calls, arguing that trial court had not adequately considered child’s tender age, education, safety, and emotional well-being.

▪️However, husband submitted an affidavit stating that he had paid the maintenance due towards the child. He further contended that wife had obstructed his attempts to meet their daughter despite the visitation order.

Allahabad High Court granted bail to a man accused of rape on the false pretext of marriage u/s 69 BNS by a transgender woman, holding that a transgender woman, even after undergoing sex-reassignment surgery, would not fall within the statutory definition of ‘woman’. 

As per the FIR, a transgender woman, had been in a relationship with applicant for more than 1.5 years on his promise to marry her. She alleged that accused subsequently refused to marry her after taking more than ₹5 lakh and had established a physical relationship with her on the false promise of marriage.

However, applicant’s counsel submitted that complainant had stated in her statements u/s 180 and 183 BNSS that she was male at birth and had undergone vulval reconstruction surgery on April 11, 2023.

Relying on a medical panel report dated August 19, 2026, applicant’s counsel contended that the complainant was a male who had undergone genital reconstruction surgery and did not have a uterus. It was argued that Section 69 BNS applies to sexual intercourse with a woman by employing deceitful means or making a promise to marry without any intention of fulfilling it, and statutory definition of ‘woman’ u/s 2(35) BNS refers to a female human being.

Court held that the expression ‘woman’ under Section 69 BNS covers only a female human being and does not include a transgender woman for the purposes of that provision.

Accordingly, Court held that, prima facie, no offence u/s 69 BNS was made out and granted bail to the applicant.
